bug_semantics: `load_rehab_pile_dataset` downloads or reuses caller-supplied `.npy` files and passes them to `numpy.load(..., allow_pickle=True)` before authenticating or validating their contents. A malicious object-array `.npy` can therefore invoke an arbitrary pickle reducer during `np.load`, executing attacker-controlled code in the Aeon caller's process; the later `.tolist()`/`np.array()` conversion occurs after deserialization and cannot mitigate execution that has already happened.
flaw_origin: The unsafe mechanism originated in the first member commit of PR #2993, `a9af1651c748e00dc735894a8b2d04b75429a498`, which created `aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py` and introduced both `np.load(..., allow_pickle=True)` calls in the then-named `load_rehabpile` function. The following member `86126a73bc3eeb2f4a642a2d6d0e3ca24922df0e` only applied formatting while retaining those calls; squash commit `0808bb1f585fbc31627fcc04254b78990d566a20` carried the mechanism onto main, where later renaming/refactoring produced `load_rehab_pile_dataset`. Commit `751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015` removed pickle enablement, but `a86b826aa7911266bb0e8f1dcd1befac6ea7b5bf` restored it four days later.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object for `a9af1651c748e00dc735894a8b2d04b75429a498` identifies the human GitHub user `sarthakuwar` (`sarthakkuwar`) as both author and committer, has subject `FEAT: Add RehabPile dataset collection and loader`, an empty body, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, no AI-tool disclosure, and no AI/bot author or committer identity.
evidence: First-party advisories: ZDI-26-468/CVE-2026-18285 names `load_rehab_pile_dataset`, untrusted-data deserialization, and arbitrary code execution, and points to the vendor update: https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-468/ ; GitHub advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-88rp-m596-52gg .

Squash decomposition: PR #2993 is https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/pull/2993 and its two-member patch series is https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/pull/2993.patch . Member `a9af1651c748e00dc735894a8b2d04b75429a498` adds `aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py` as a new file and first writes the two `np.load(..., allow_pickle=True)` calls: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/a9af1651c748e00dc735894a8b2d04b75429a498 . Member `86126a73bc3eeb2f4a642a2d6d0e3ca24922df0e` is automatic formatting and preserves them. The main-history squash is `0808bb1f585fbc31627fcc04254b78990d566a20`: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/0808bb1f585fbc31627fcc04254b78990d566a20 .

Direct-parent verification: the BIC object records sole parent `96aff5a386d6719ef83dfc8aeb1fc1932cf8e539`; requesting `aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py` from that exact parent tree returns 404, while the BIC diff is `new file mode 100644`: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/96aff5a386d6719ef83dfc8aeb1fc1932cf8e539/aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py . Thus the vulnerable loader and lines are absent in the immediate parent.

BIC-only attribution evidence: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/a9af1651c748e00dc735894a8b2d04b75429a498.json records author and committer `sarthakuwar`/`sarthakkuwar`, `isGitHub:false`, subject `FEAT: Add RehabPile dataset collection and loader`, empty body, and parent `96aff5a386d6719ef83dfc8aeb1fc1932cf8e539`; the patch header gives author `sarthakkuwar <kuwarsarthak711@gmail.com>`: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/a9af1651c748e00dc735894a8b2d04b75429a498.patch . No commit-object AI marker is present.

Direct fix: advisory-referenced commit `751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015` changes `aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py` by replacing both `np.load(..., allow_pickle=True)` calls with default `np.load(...)`, preventing object-pickle loading: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015 . Its exact parent is `ee58d0c290a9360bda414235bfd18b88b728b8b2`, whose file still contains the vulnerable calls.

Fix regression/current exposure: `a86b826aa7911266bb0e8f1dcd1befac6ea7b5bf` explicitly restores `allow_pickle=True` for X and y after the temporary fix: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/a86b826aa7911266bb0e8f1dcd1befac6ea7b5bf . Assigned-clone HEAD `13f10b2a33f4476a794891b1a13d2b4a737f5b82` still has the unsafe calls at `aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py:292-294`.

Released-version boundary: v1.2.0 (`d8dc31f46ece4101e0cf97a427d79a73477d0a42`) predates the BIC and has no `rehabpile_loader.py` (404). v1.3.0 (`c80baf772dcf0e60aaaae87c27d1befdef90a7b4`) and v1.4.0 (`53cd01894e52552c2cf141c22d73199c488e14e6`) contain both `allow_pickle=True` calls. The historical fix landed after v1.4.0, but the reintroduction landed before v1.5.0; v1.5.0 (`e5c37bb0a54950b552df33546c47510fffa0752b`) also contains the unsafe calls: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/v1.3.0/aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/v1.4.0/aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/v1.5.0/aeon/datasets/rehabpile_loader.py . Therefore the released affected boundary is v1.3.0 through latest release v1.5.0, with no durable patched release. GitHub's advisory independently lists affected and patched versions as unknown.
reasoning: The audit starts from the advisory's named sink and follows the exact pickle-enabling lines rather than treating later moves, renames, or the squash aggregate as the introducer. PR #2993 is reconstructable as two member commits. Its first member `a9af1651c748e00dc735894a8b2d04b75429a498` creates the loader and writes the unsafe calls; its exact parent lacks the entire file, while the second member only formats the already-vulnerable implementation. The squash `0808bb1f585fbc31627fcc04254b78990d566a20` is therefore landing evidence, not the smallest BIC. Tag trees establish that v1.2.0 is unaffected because the loader does not exist, and that v1.3.0 and v1.4.0 are affected. The advisory-linked `751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015` is a direct mechanism fix, but `a86b826aa7911266bb0e8f1dcd1befac6ea7b5bf` reintroduced the same lines before v1.5.0, making v1.5.0 and current main vulnerable and leaving no patched release boundary. Finally, attribution is based solely on the decomposed BIC commit object: it has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any AI activity elsewhere in the repository or release history.
remaining_gap: No durable vendor patch or patched release boundary currently exists: the direct fix `751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015` was undone by `a86b826aa7911266bb0e8f1dcd1befac6ea7b5bf`, and both v1.5.0 and assigned-clone HEAD remain vulnerable.
